paragraphs: Rav Chiyya, son of Avin (the carpenter), student of Shmuel; see above. He said, “I asked Rav Adda bar Ahavah”—Shabbat 140a. He said to Rav Acha bar Yosef: there. Rav Idi, his brother. “R. Elazar teaches us in the name of R. Chanina the Great”—Yevamot 43a. “R. Huna said”—Taanit 8a. He asked Rav Huna: Kiddushin 58a, near the end. “I asked Rav Huna”—Shabbat 140a. He said to Rav Huna bar Chinena. R. Zeira rode a donkey and R. Chiyya bar Avin walked behind him. He said, “Is it certain that you said in R. Yochanan's name ...?”: Berakhot 33b. In Rav Chisda's name; and he asked Rav Chisda—Menachot 49a. “Rav Yehudah said”—Moed Katan 16a. “R. Yehoshua ben Korcha said”—Megillah 14a; Gittin 57b; Nazir 23b, near the end; Bava Batra 91b; Horayot 11a. Yoma 39b: R. Yehoshua ben Korcha said, “An old man told me that he smelled the scent of incense in the walls of Shiloh.” “R. Yochanan said”—Eruvin 47b; Megillah 6b; Nazir 61a. He asked Rav Yosef: Sanhedrin 83b. “R. Nechemyah bar Barukh said: R. Chiyya bar Avin said.” Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak asked R. Chiyya bar Avin. “R. Amram said”—Bekhorot 18a. “Rav said: R. Chiyya bar Avin said: Rav Amram said”—Yevamot 25b. The words “Rav said” are a scribal error; it should read “R. Chiyya bar Avin said.” “R. Chiyya bar Avin said: Rav Amram was sitting when Rav Sheshet said”—see there—Ketubot 11b. “Rav said”—Gittin 40a; Eruvin 81a. Whether he was Rav's student requires investigation. It seems he was not his student, nor Shmuel's student, although he spoke in their names. Rava said, “I and the lion of the company explained it.” Who was this? R. Chiyya bar Avin: end of Shemonah Sheratzim; Kiddushin 48b; Sanhedrin 8b. Responsa Bach, section 55, writes that he was Rava's student, since he asked Rava in Nedarim 34b, and that the law follows Rava against R. Chiyya bar Avin because he was his student; see there, and Rava. This requires investigation: since he was Shmuel's and Rav Huna's student, how could he be Rava's student? Rav Huna died before Rav Yehudah, and Rava was born when Rav Yehudah died. As for the proof that asking Rava makes him his student, I already wrote in the general rules that this is not necessary. Furthermore, Rava called him “the lion of the company.” Rava bar Sheilta said to him. “Shmuel said”—Shabbat 52a, 129a; Eruvin 79b; Beitzah 9a, 39a; Kiddushin 72a–b; Bava Metzia 100a. Rav Amram was sitting when Rav Sheshet spoke; see above.
